title: Ethiopian Thick Fermented Grain Drink
community: Southern Ethiopia — the thick fermented drink of the Gurage and others
author: Mama Tigist

heritage.origin: Gurage people and southern Ethiopia — the thick nutritive fermented drink
heritage.history: Borde is a thick, highly nutritious fermented drink made from a mixture of maize, wheat, barley, and other grains — it is simultaneously a drink and a food, consumed particularly by those who need maximum nutrition quickly. Associated with the Gurage people but consumed across southern Ethiopia, borde is given to those doing heavy physical work, to those recovering from illness, and to nursing mothers. It is more nutritious than tella (thicker, more grain solids) and is not consumed for pleasure alone but for sustenance.

desc: Ethiopian Borde — a thick, opaque fermented drink made from multiple grains (maize, wheat, barley) cooked, cooled, and fermented for 1—2 days. More nutritious than tella — consumed for sustenance by labourers, the sick, and nursing mothers. Southern Ethiopia's most nourishing traditional drink.
longDesc: Borde is the drinkable food of southern Ethiopia — thicker than tella, more nutritious, and fermented for a shorter time. It is consumed cold, often strained to different thicknesses.
ingredients: 100ml borde starter (previous batch) or active yeast
steps: Mix all flours. Add 1 litre water. Cook, stirring, 15—18 minutes until thick.
Add remaining 2 litres cold water. Mix well.
chefTips: Borde is meant to be thick — strain less than tella.
The pre-cooking of the flour gelatinises the starches before fermentation.
cookingScience: Cooking the flour before fermentation gelatinises the starch — making it more readily fermentable by the naturally occurring lactic acid bacteria and yeasts. The resulting beverage contains both alcohol and significant unfermented starch (the thicker solids) — making it simultaneously alcoholic and nourishing.
sustainabilityTips: Uses multiple locally grown grains — excellent dietary diversity.
servedWith: As a nutritive drink for labourers
culturalNote: Borde is the drink of effort — given to the farmer who has worked the highland fields since dawn, to the labourer who carries heavy loads, to the mother who has given birth. It is sustenance as generosity.
